audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Josiah covenant, religious purge, Passover, death at Megiddo, Jehoahaz removal, and Jehoiakim taxation narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for public scroll reading, covenant renewal, removal and destruction of sacred objects, qadesh terminology, women textile workers, Topheth and child protection, religious-site defilement, grave and bone desecration, execution of high-place priests, Passover, spirit-practitioner suppression, unmatched royal praise, unresolved collective wrath, Josiah's violent death, Egyptian imperial intervention, forced renaming, tribute, and taxation.

verses.restored: King sent, and they gathered to him all elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

King went up to house of YHWH, and with him every man of Judah, all inhabitants of Jerusalem, priests, prophets, and all people, from small to great. He read in their ears all words of scroll of covenant found in house of YHWH.

King stood by pillar and cut covenant before YHWH, to walk after YHWH and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all heart and all soul, to establish words of this covenant written in this scroll. All people stood in covenant.

King commanded Hilkiah the high priest, priests of second rank, and guardians of threshold to bring from temple of YHWH all vessels made for Baal, Asherah, and all host of heavens. He burned them outside Jerusalem in fields of Kidron and carried their dust to Bethel.

He removed the appointed idolatrous priests whom kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense at high places in cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations, and all host of heavens.
He brought Asherah from house of YHWH outside Jerusalem to wadi Kidron, burned it at wadi Kidron, ground it to dust, and threw its dust upon graves of children of people.
He tore down houses of qadesh by house of YHWH, where women were weaving houses/hangings for Asherah.

He brought all priests from cities of Judah and defiled high places where priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer-sheba. He tore down high places of gates at entrance of gate of Joshua governor of city, which were on left of a man at city gate.
Only priests of high places did not go up to altar of YHWH in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
He defiled Topheth in valley of sons of Hinnom, so no man would make his son or daughter pass through fire to Molech.
He removed horses kings of Judah had given to sun, from entrance of house of YHWH by chamber of Nathan-melech the court official in colonnades, and burned chariots of sun with fire.

Altars upon roof of upper room of Ahaz, which kings of Judah had made, and altars Manasseh made in two courts of house of YHWH, king broke down and ran from there, and threw their dust into wadi Kidron.

High places east of Jerusalem, south of Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel built for Ashtoreth deity of Sidonians, Chemosh deity of Moab, and Milcom deity of children of Ammon, king defiled.
He broke pillars, cut down Asherim, and filled their places with human bones.
Also altar at Bethel and high place Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made—both altar and high place he tore down. He burned high place, ground it to dust, and burned Asherah.

Josiah turned and saw graves there in mountain. He sent, took bones from graves, and burned them upon altar, defiling it according to word of YHWH proclaimed by man of Divine who proclaimed these things.
He said, What is this marker I see? Men of city said to him, It is grave of man of Divine who came from Judah and proclaimed these things you did against altar of Bethel.
He said, Let him rest; let no man move his bones. So they let his bones escape, with bones of prophet who came from Samaria.
Josiah also removed all houses of high places in cities of Samaria, which kings of Israel had made to provoke, and did to them according to all deeds he did at Bethel.
He slaughtered all priests of high places who were there upon altars and burned human bones upon them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
King commanded all people, saying, Make Passover to YHWH your Divine, as written in this scroll of covenant.
For such a Passover had not been made from days of judges who judged Israel, nor all days of kings of Israel and kings of Judah.
But in eighteenth year of king Josiah this Passover was made to YHWH in Jerusalem.

Also mediums, spirit-knowers, household gods, idols, and all detestable things seen in land of Judah and Jerusalem Josiah removed, to establish words of Torah written in scroll Hilkiah the priest found in house of YHWH.
Before him there was no king like him who turned to YHWH with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might, according to all Torah of Moses; and after him none arose like him.
Yet YHWH did not turn from burning of his great anger, by which his anger burned against Judah because of all provocations by which Manasseh provoked him.
YHWH said, I will also remove Judah from before my face as I removed Israel; I will reject this city Jerusalem I chose and house of which I said, My name shall be there.
Remaining acts of Josiah and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to king of Assyria at river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Neco put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.

His servants carried him dead in chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his grave. People of land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
Twenty-three years old was Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to all his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Neco confined him at Riblah in land of Hamath so he would not reign in Jerusalem, and placed upon land tribute of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz, who came to Egypt and died there.

Jehoiakim gave silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed land to give silver according to command of Pharaoh. From people of land, each according to his assessment, he exacted silver and gold to give to Pharaoh Neco.
Twenty-five years old was Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to all his fathers had done.

translation_notes: Public reading and covenant renewal include elders, priests, prophets, and all people, but royal leadership and crowd participation do not guarantee free consent or ethically valid implementation.

Josiah's reform includes destruction, burning, defilement, and forced closure of other sacred practices. It is a major religious-violence text and may not authorize persecution, vandalism, desecration, or coerced conversion.

The Hebrew qadesh in verse 7 refers to a class of cult personnel and must not be rendered or weaponized as a generic slur against gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, queer, or gender-nonconforming people.
The women weaving for Asherah are skilled religious textile workers. Their labor and livelihoods must not disappear beneath the king's destruction of their workplace.

Topheth is disabled so children cannot be passed through fire. Preventing child sacrifice is ethically necessary, but child protection does not legitimate every violent act performed under the same reform.
Filling shrines with bones, opening graves, burning remains, and using corpses to defile altars are desecration of the dead. Prophetic fulfillment does not make grave violation good.
Josiah executes priests of high places without narrated trial. Religious office or belief never warrants summary killing.
Passover is Jewish covenantal practice. This account may not support Christian supersessionism, appropriation that erases Judaism, or coercion of Jews or others.
The removal of mediums and spirit-knowers may not support witch-hunts, occult panic, or violence toward contemporary spiritual practitioners.
Josiah is praised as unmatched in turning to YHWH, yet collective wrath remains. This exposes a morally troubling theology in which present reform does not spare later people from prior royal wrongs.
Huldah's promise that Josiah would be gathered in peace stands in tension with his death at Megiddo. The textual-theological tension must remain visible.

Egyptian power confines Jehoahaz, forcibly renames and installs Jehoiakim, imposes tribute, and drives taxation of the population. Puppet rule and imperial finance are central to the chapter's ending.
safety_note: Do not imitate Josiah's religious purge, target LGBTQ people through qadesh mistranslation, destroy sacred sites, desecrate graves, execute clergy or spiritual practitioners, or erase Jewish ownership of Passover. Preserve child protection, women's labor, bodily dignity, Huldah's unresolved oracle, and the population taxed and ruled beneath Egyptian imperial control.
